title: Reduction to extensions by zero and the Hom formula
statement:
Use the standing scheme setting [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting]: $\ell$ is prime, $k$ is a field of characteristic $p>0$ with $p\ne\ell$, and $X$ is separated of finite type over $k$. Fix a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\pi_E$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Use the pulled-back condensed coefficient sheaf $\mathcal O_{E,T}$ on each small pro-étale site $T_{\mathrm{proét}}$ [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients, def-weil-pbc-small-proetale-site], and the categories $\Cons,\Dbc$ of [sk-def-sfb-constructible]. Work in the ambient unbounded module derived categories, with inverse/direct images as in [sk-def-sfb-module-pushforward-pullback], and the ordinary, uncompleted relative derived tensor and derived internal Hom of [sk-def-sfb-derived-tensor-hom], in the size convention [def-weil-size-convention]. Write $R\operatorname{Hom}_T(A,B)=R\Gamma(T,R\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O_{E,T}}(A,B))$ for global derived Hom, with derived sections as in [def-pur-ringed-site-zeroth-hypercohomology].

1. Every $C\in\Dbc(X,\mathcal O_E)$ admits a finite filtration by distinguished triangles [def-weil-triangulated-category] whose graded pieces are shifts of objects $a_!L$, where $a=i\circ u:S\hookrightarrow X$ is the inclusion of a stratum of a finite stratification [def-constructible-stratification], with $u:S\hookrightarrow Z$ open and $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ closed [def-weil-open-immersion, def-weil-closed-immersion]. Here $a_!:=i_*u_!$, with $u_!$ extension by zero [def-sfb-module-open-lower-shriek], and $L\in\Cons(S,\mathcal O_E)$ is pro-étale locally the completion of a finitely generated $\mathcal O_E$-module, meaning $\mathcal O_{E,S}\otimes_{\underline{\mathcal O_E}}\underline M$ for such an $M$. If $C\in\Cons(X,\mathcal O_E)$, the pieces may be taken in degree $0$.
2. For such $a,L$, let $R\underline\Gamma_Z:D(X_{\mathrm{proét}},\mathcal O_E)\to D(Z_{\mathrm{proét}},\mathcal O_E)$ be the derived support functor of [det-lem-formal-closed-support-derived], and put
$$L^\vee:=R\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O_{E,S}}(L,\mathcal O_{E,S}).$$
For every $K\in D(X_{\mathrm{proét}},\mathcal O_E)$ there is a natural isomorphism
$$R\operatorname{Hom}_X(a_!L,K)\simeq R\Gamma\bigl(S,L^\vee\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{\mathcal O_{E,S}}u^*R\underline\Gamma_ZK\bigr).$$
The object $L^\vee$ has Tor amplitude contained in $[0,1]$ (Tor amplitude as in [sk-def-sfb-constructible]). Tensoring with it commutes with small filtered colimits of complexes and with countable derived inverse limits. Filtered colimits are represented by degreewise colimits of module-sheaf complexes [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]; derived inverse limits refer to strict inverse systems of such complexes, with their total derived inverse limit and Roos triangle [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit, def-weil-derived-limit].

proof.text: The finite-type scheme is Noetherian by the Mathlib finite-type and Noetherian APIs. Bounded constructibility already supplies boundedness and constant-model constructibility of each cohomology sheaf. Choose the finite family of degrees in a bounded interval; outside it the cohomology is zero.

Apply the common-reduced-stratification theorem to that finite family. Its ordered reduced strata have open prefix unions and reduced closed tails. Their restrictions all have finite constant local models. Fixed-strata localization generation expresses each degree-zero cohomology sheaf in the extension closure of its stratum extensions by zero.

Shift the generation property by minus the cohomological degree. If the original complex is concentrated in degree zero, each other cohomology sheaf vanishes; all retained stratum shifts are therefore zero. Apply bounded degreewise devissage to the isomorphism-invariant extension closure. Triangle-extension associativity flattens each finite extension product into a finite chain with zero initial vertex. Treat the zero complex by the empty chain.

Use the local resolution of a finite constant integral model by two dualizable terms. Transport the derived mapping-cone dualizability and Tor amplitude [-1,0] through its cokernel isomorphism in the abstract category, then specialize to coefficient modules. Dualizability descends along the pro-etale cover. The Tor component of the existing local-duality-descent theorem supplies the same global Tor bound. Choose a right dual and use the derived braiding to obtain the reverse exact pairing. The tensor adjunction and uniqueness of right adjoints identify internal Hom from the original object with tensor by that chosen dual. Evaluation at the unit identifies the recorded internal dual with the chosen dual. Transport its exact pairing and Tor amplitude [0,1] to the recorded dual. Tensor by it also preserves small limits.

The module kernel support construction is right adjoint to exact closed pushforward, by the sheaf support argument and closed/open detection. It is additive. Compare this adjunction with canonical closed support. Apply the closed and open internal Hom formulas. For every scheme morphism, the ordinary adjunction identifies sections of direct image with sections, and exact inverse image implies preservation of K-injectives by the right adjoint. Derive these comparisons and compose them with the dual-tensor comparison to obtain the natural global Hom formula.

Essential surjectivity of localization on K-flat complexes gives a K-flat representative of the dual. The monoidal localization lifting comparison identifies its complex-level tensor functor followed by localization with derived tensor by the dual. Tensor by a complex has an internal-Hom right adjoint, hence preserves all small colimits and in particular filtered degreewise colimits.

Dual tensor is exact, commutes with shifts and preserves products. Map any distinguished strict-tower Roos triangle through it. The product comparison isomorphism identifies every mapped projection with the canonical projection; consequently it identifies the mapped successor difference with the successor difference of the mapped tower. Transport the mapped distinguished triangle along this product comparison to obtain the asserted derived-limit triangle and projection map.

lean.note: Both clauses are in lean.declarations. The filtration has one common finite stratification and actual distinguished triangles, with zero shifts for degree-zero inputs. The formula is a natural isomorphism in the arbitrary unbounded target. Filtered colimits are degreewise colimits on a K-flat tensor model, not ordinary categorical colimits in a triangulated category. The strict-tower clause preserves the Roos triangle with its induced projection map. The added landed coefficient-data node supplies canonical aliases without a new coefficient construction. The three generic stratumModule constructions keep coefficients abstract before integral specialization; the existing specialized definitions delegate to precisely these constructions. See the definition-change records.
